task: Make open-summary completeness and checker occurrence completeness independently verifiable while preserving already admitted checked-body producers.
observation: The strict occurrence ledger exposed valid generic field and constructor shapes whose checker path had not retained a field receiver child, nominal field identity, constructor field ordinal, or a useful source/result TypeRef. Requiring the old open-summary complete bit to imply a complete occurrence graph also broke existing bounded H3/M2b producers before their replacement lowerer had parity.
impact: Separating the open type/effect/dependency summary from occurrence-ledger completeness preserved the existing admitted source-free corpus while keeping the missing checker facts explicitly unavailable to the generic occurrence lowerer.

resolution.summary: Checker-owned field receiver, field declaration identity/ordinal, arithmetic result TypeRefs, deferred Count stage TypeRefs, and constructor field ordinals are retained; open summaries and occurrence-ledger completeness now have separate gates. The M2b2 source-free corpus passes on this tree.

task: Make public callable completeness require the full checker occurrence ledger without disabling independently guarded body producers.
observation: The architect found that a generic summary could be exposed as complete when its type scheme, effects, and dependencies were resolved but its body occurrence ledger was not. The first strict-gating edit also showed that the generalized lowering path had not preserved the source-free parameter-return producer; projecting its existing checker-retained result through the canonical checked-body reader restored the corpus controls. A valid multi-statement generic arithmetic probe still has no complete summary because its inferred local return and operator facts are not yet retained as one callable scheme.
impact: The public complete flag now includes occurrence-ledger and occurrence-dependency completeness, while narrow producers continue to use scheme eligibility only with their shape and canonical-body checks. The remaining multi-statement inference gap stays fail-closed and is not represented as supported.

resolution.summary: Strict public completeness and parameter-return compatibility are covered. A two-statement generic arithmetic body now retains result/operation facts, emits a canonical source-free record, projects after source removal, and survives legacy-body poisoning; broader control-flow and producer parity remain open.

task: Advance checker-owned control-flow facts and the shared checked-body producer/importer path.
observation: A direct-return-only importer could not project the newly retained two-statement arithmetic body, and a branch-local name had no exact identity after an if/else join. The shared reader already validates these nodes, but source-free coverage needed an occurrence-based record path and a checker-owned join binding.
impact: A source-free generic provider now emits and imports the two-statement arithmetic body and an if/else body whose branches return. The branch-join ledger retains a unique join identity and TypeRef, while unimplemented statement families remain unavailable.

resolution.summary: Focused new corpus rows pass, but full generic language coverage and one record builder/reader route across all producers remain open R1 work.
